chunks: Al-Shaykh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me; he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid informed me, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar and Ahmad ibn Idris, both together, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi al-'Ala' — or another — transmitting it in elevated form (marfu'an). He said:

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, peace be upon him, was asked: 'What is the ruling (hadd) for relieving oneself?' He said: 'Do not face the qibla, and do not turn your back to it; do not face the wind, and do not turn your back to it.'

As for the hadith narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who said: 'I entered upon Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha, peace be upon him, and in his house there was a toilet (kanif) facing the qibla' —

— it is to be understood as meaning: if a toilet was built facing this direction without choice, then there is no harm in sitting upon it out of necessity. Moreover, the report does not state that he saw him [the Imam] during defecation or urination facing the qibla or with his back to it; rather, he said only: 'I saw a toilet in his house with this characteristic.' It is moreover possible that it was constructed without his permission — that is, the house may have passed into his possession already built in this manner — and this nullifies relying on this report as evidence.

Then al-Shaykh said: It is not appropriate for him to speak while relieving himself, except when necessity compels him to do so, or when he mentions Allah the Exalted and praises Him, or when he hears mention of the Messenger and sends blessings upon him and upon his family, and whatever resembles that from among what is obligatory in all circumstances — and this [preceding ruling] indicates that [i.e., supports the present ruling].

key_terms.الضَّرُورَةُ: necessity; a compelling need that may relax an otherwise prohibited act
key_terms.الْغَائِطِ: defecation; the act of answering the call of nature
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: qibla; the direction of prayer toward the Ka'ba in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on facing the qibla while relieving oneself according to Imam al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (AS) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (AS) was asked about the proper rule (hadd) for relieving oneself, and he replied that one must neither face the qibla nor turn one's back to it, and likewise must neither face the wind nor turn one's back to it. The text then reconciles a seemingly contradictory narration about a toilet facing the qibla in Imam al-Ridha's (AS) home, arguing the report describes only the structural orientation of the latrine—not the Imam's actual posture—and that it may have been built without his consent. Al-Shaykh concludes with a general ruling that speaking while relieving oneself is discouraged except under necessity or for obligatory remembrances such as praising Allah or sending blessings upon the Prophet and his family.
